criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 reading: Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, yes—the paper examines institutional and governance processes, specifically top-down infrastructure project implementation by the national water utility (AyA) and institutionalized conflict-resolution mechanisms (direct negotiation via a technical commission and facilitation by the Defensoría de los Habitantes). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism clarification, no—it examines conflict negotiation and citizen participation around bulk water-infrastructure siting/delivery rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community service access (eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements, tariff/cost-recovery rules, discretion/accommodation, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure governing service access). evidence_quotes.quote: This triggered a dispute over the control of the water sources, which confronted Government institutions and the Atenas and Tacares communities. This article focuses both in the dispute itself and in Government-led attempts to find a negotiated solution to the conflict.

Para esto se caracterizan los actores presentes en las distintas negociaciones entre las partes, las estrategias empleadas en cada caso, y finalmente, la pertinencia o no de este tipo de respuestas institucionales para el procesamiento de demandas políticas ante un conflicto por el uso y gestión de un recurso natural de vital importancia: el agua.

Para los vecinos de Tacares, la causa del conflicto era la implementación de un proyecto con las características de una política pública top-down pues la formulación y el inicio de su ejecución fue a través de una imposición institucional;

Para esto se emplea un diseño de investigación cualitativo a través de entrevistas semiestructuradas a actores de la comunidad de Tacares y a actores institucionales; asimismo se realiza una revisión bibliográfica de actas institucionales y de publicaciones en medios de comunicación locales y nacionales.

Finalmente, tras examinar el conflicto y las negociaciones se concluye, por un lado, que durante este proceso se reproducen las distintas asimetrías de poder entre actores, y, por otro, que el argumento de fomentar la participación solo se utiliza cuando los conflictos han escalado.

raw_response.exposure: Top-down implementation of an inter-cantonal water-capture infrastructure project (Mejoras al Sistema de Abastecimiento de Atenas) by AyA and subsequent conflict-negotiation processes (direct negotiation with Comisión Técnica Negociadora and facilitation by Defensoría de los Habitantes)
raw_response.outcome: Socio-environmental conflict and negotiation outcomes: failure to ratify a negotiated consensus, completion of the infrastructure project in 2019 as originally designed, community adoption of technical framing, and reproduction of power asymmetries between state and community actors
raw_response.population_and_sample: Community actors in Tacares (Grecia canton, Alajuela province) and institutional officials of the Instituto Costarricense de Acueductos y Alcantarillados (AyA), Costa Rica (qualitative case study citing 4 key-informant interviews conducted in 2019 plus institutional minutes and media reports; unit of analysis: socio-environmental conflict and negotiation process)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded as E01 (Wrong topic), with concurrent failure on C2 (narrow rule-type exposure) and C4 (service-access outcome). Although water rationing in Atenas is noted as background context for why Costa Rica's water utility (AyA) initiated a bulk water-transfer infrastructure project in 2012, this political-science qualitative case study investigates socio-environmental conflict, social mobilization, and state-community negotiation processes over tapping natural springs in Parque Recreativo Municipal Los Chorros (Tacares), rather than household or community water service access (c1=no). Under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification, it examines top-down project delivery and conflict-negotiation/facilitation processes rather than a rule-type legal or administrative mechanism governing household or community service access (c2=no). Finally, its empirical findings concern negotiation dynamics, technical framing, and power asymmetries rather than water access, connection, reliability, quantity, or affordability outcomes (c4=no).
